tracks.name: Well-rounded software engineer
tracks.blurb: The full spine, in order. Slowest route, widest ceiling. Pick this if you don't yet know what you want to build.

tracks.name: Learn Python properly (no career pressure)
tracks.blurb: Language, engineering habits and problem solving, with automation as the payoff. Stops before the infrastructure-heavy phases.

tracks.name: Backend & API engineer
tracks.blurb: Databases, HTTP services, auth, containers and deployment. The most common professional Python job.

tracks.name: Data analysis & data engineering
tracks.blurb: SQL first, then pipelines, warehouses and orchestration. Heavy on correctness and schema design.

tracks.name: AI & machine learning engineer
tracks.blurb: The maths and the plumbing. You still need the engineering phases — an unshippable model is a hobby.

tracks.name: Automation, scripting & scraping
tracks.blurb: Make the computer do the boring parts. Short path to something useful, then hardening so it survives real failure.

tracks.name: DevOps & platform engineering
tracks.blurb: Linux, networking, containers, pipelines and the operational surface underneath everything else.

tracks.name: Application security
tracks.blurb: You cannot secure what you cannot build. Build the app, then learn to break it.

tracks.name: Job-ready in the shortest honest time
tracks.blurb: Language, data structures, algorithms, SQL and one shipped, tested, deployed service. Optimised for passing a real hiring loop.
